title: Cold rebuild: Read `kubectl get pods`
summary: Rebuild Read `kubectl get pods` from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Read `kubectl get pods`** in *kubectl, namespaces and contexts*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A container restarts every minute. `kubectl logs web-1` shows only the startup banner of the *new* attempt. How do you see the output of the attempt that crashed?
steps.explain: `--previous` (or `-p`) shows the logs of the last terminated container instance, which is usually where the stack trace is.

steps.title: Rebuild Read `kubectl get pods` cold
prompt: Write `List<string> NotReady(string output)` that takes the text of `kubectl get pods` (header line first) and returns the names of pods that are **not fully ready**: the two numbers in `READY` differ, or `STATUS` is not `Running` or `Completed`.
returns `["web-2"]`. A `Completed` pod shows `0/1` but is healthy (its work is done). Columns are separated by one or more spaces.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
